title: DeployMocks has no block.chainid guard at all, in direct contravention of the project's own CLAUDE.md, while every DeployMainnet* script carries one twice
propagation: LOCAL-ONLY (the guard's absence is the finding; the port must add one)
specText: Story 073 line 66: 'No mainnet contact of any kind. Everything here targets chainId **31337**.'
specConformanceLabel: F-05 (cross-reference only — primary home is the QA/Low bundle)
faithfulnessRouting: F-05 — CROSS-REFERENCE ONLY. Primary home remains the QA/Low bundle; listed in the spec-conformance report so the story-level deviation is visible to the owner, but NOT counted twice in the severity totals.
description: Line :290 merely LOGS the chain id. There is no `require(block.chainid == 31337)` anywhere in the 1946-line file. All seven DeployMainnet* scripts carry `require(block.chainid == 1)`, most of them twice (setUp + run). The project's own CLAUDE.md is explicit: 'Anvil may relax these checks for local iteration, but the relaxation must be gated behind an explicit `block.chainid == 31337` branch and clearly commented — never share an unsafe default code path between local and real networks.' The same file also lists 'Mock contracts with unlimited minting / Default Anvil private keys / Unrestricted permissions / Simplified initialization' under 'Local Development Only — NEVER deploy these configurations to Sepolia or Mainnet.'
impact: Story 073 enlarges the ungated surface: unrestricted `MockKendu.mint`, `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` granted at :1648 and :1731 and never revoked (verified live: `authorizedMinters(deployer) == (true, 1)` after the run), the 300-ETH `WETH9.deposit` at :1460, real `PhusdStableMinter.mint` calls in Phases 9/9.5/9.55/9.6, and the entire destructive V1-staker teardown (pause + pauser repoint to an EOA + unregister from the global Pauser). The only thing preventing this script from running against a non-anvil RPC is the operator typing the right --rpc-url. This is a footgun in the Law-3 sense: a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised that the one script in the repo containing every unsafe local relaxation is also the only one with no chain gate.
attackPath: No attack path. Line :290 merely LOGS block.chainid; there is no `require(block.chainid == 31337)` anywhere in the 1946-line file, while all seven DeployMainnet* scripts carry `require(block.chainid == 1)`, most of them twice.
evidence: grep for `block.chainid` in script/DeployMocks.s.sol returns a single hit at :290, inside a console.log. grep for `setMinter(.*false)` returns nothing. Live post-run: `cast call MockPhUSD 'authorizedMinters(address)' 0xf39Fd6e5… -> (true, 1)`, `mintVersion() -> 1`.
recommendation: Add `require(block.chainid == 31337, "DeployMocks: anvil only")` in `run()` before `vm.startBroadcast`. Independently, revoke the two `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` grants at the end of the run and post-assert `authorizedMinters(deployer).canMint == false`, so the port inherits a revoke-and-assert habit rather than a standing grant.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal, and explicitly NOT escalated. The aggravating context is real and unusually heavy - this is the one script in the repo carrying every documented unsafe local relaxation (unrestricted MockKendu.mint, the 300-ETH WETH9.deposit at :1460, real PhusdStableMinter.mint calls in Phases 9/9.5/9.55/9.6, and the destructive V1-staker teardown that pauses, repoints the pauser to an EOA and unregisters from the global Pauser) and it directly contravenes the project's own CLAUDE.md rule that the anvil relaxation 'must be gated behind an explicit block.chainid == 31337 branch'. But severity must follow demonstrated impact, not the size of the hypothetical: no asset is at risk on the actual entry point, the misuse required is obvious rather than non-obvious, and the mocks deployed on a wrong chain would not be the real contracts. Low is correct. HIGHEST-VALUE PART OF THE FIX, and the part most likely to be lost in a QA bundle: the two `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` grants at :1648 and :1731 are NEVER revoked - verified live post-run, `authorizedMinters(deployer) == (true, 1)`, and grep for `setMinter(.*false)` returns nothing. Harmless on anvil, but a standing unrevoked minter grant is exactly the habit that must not be inherited by the mainnet port. Revoke and post-assert `authorizedMinters(deployer).canMint == false`. || STORY-073 FAITHFULNESS RE-WEIGH — HELD AT LOW, CHARACTER UPGRADED. Story 073 line 66 states, as a flat property of the work, 'No mainnet contact of any kind. Everything here targets chainId 31337.' Nothing in DeployMocks.s.sol enforces it: :290 logs block.chainid and there is no require anywhere in the file. WHAT THIS CHANGES. The finding is no longer merely an intra-repo convention asymmetry ('the seven DeployMainnet* scripts guard, this one does not') plus a CLAUDE.md rule. It is now a DOCUMENTED INVARIANT THAT IS NOT HELD - the story asserts the property in the indicative, and the only thing actually holding it is the operator typing the right --rpc-url. That is a Law-2 spec deviation on its face, so the finding is tagged faithfulness:true and cross-referenced into the spec-conformance report as F-05 rather than being allowed to sit only in a QA bundle. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE - THE SEVERITY. Held at Low, deliberately and against the temptation of a three-source stack (CLAUDE.md + intra-repo asymmetry + story line 66). (1) The failure mode required is running a script literally named DeployMocks against a production RPC. Under Law 3 that is an OBVIOUS-consequence operator error, not a non-obvious footgun, and obvious misuse is out of scope by rule; only the intra-repo asymmetry is non-obvious, and asymmetry alone does not carry impact. (2) No asset is at risk on the actual entry point. (3) On a mis-pointed RPC the realistic outcome is a failed or garbage deploy - the destructive V1-staker teardown resolves its targets from local artifacts that do not exist elsewhere, and the mocks deployed would not be the real contracts. (4) Three documents all asserting the same unenforced property raise CONFIDENCE that the guard is owed and raise FIX PRIORITY; they do not manufacture impact, and severity follows demonstrated impact. Low is correct and is the ceiling this evidence supports. The highest-value part of the fix is unchanged and must not be lost in the bundle: the two `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` grants at :1648 and :1731 are never revoked - revoke them and post-assert `authorizedMinters(deployer).canMint == false`.
severityAgreement: HELD AT LOW. Character upgraded from convention-gap to documented-invariant-not-held; severity unchanged because the misuse remains obvious under Law 3.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
